title: Situation Reporting (SITREPS)

nodes.text: Initiate Situation Reporting (SITREPS)

evidence.source_text: Situation Reporting (SITREPS)

nodes.text: Provide frequent, concise situation reports

evidence.source_text: Everyone in leadership positions are required to provide frequent, concise situation reports.

nodes.text: Crew Leaders provide sitreps to fireground supervisor

evidence.source_text: Those on the fireground (for example Crew Leaders) need to recognise that it is an important part of their role to provide sitreps to their fireground supervisor.

nodes.text: Ensure critical information flow during escalating or major incident

evidence.source_text: Critical Information Flow During an Escalating or Major Incident

nodes.text: IMT generates, processes, and coordinates information for emergency management

evidence.source_text: An IMT generates, processes and coordinates much of the information needed for successful emergency management.

nodes.text: Information flows between fireground and IMT, and from IMT to regional and state levels

evidence.source_text: Information flows between the fireground and the IMT, and from the IMT to the regional and state levels of control.

nodes.text: Integrate information with other stakeholders (medical services, critical infrastructure, other agencies, police)

evidence.source_text: In addition, there is also a need to integrate information with other stakeholders such as providers of medical services, critical infrastructure, other agencies and the police.

nodes.text: Use AIIMS for effective and efficient control of incidents

evidence.source_text: AIIMS assists with the effective and efficient control of incidents by providing structures for communication and information flow.

nodes.text: Use AIIMS tools for common communications framework and integration

evidence.source_text: There are a variety of tools embedded within AIIMS that provide a common communications framework to enhance integration, including an IAP used to generate and communicate intent.
